title.en: Was, were: the past of be
title.sl: Was, were (preteklik od be): I was, you were
title.de: Was, were (die Vergangenheit von be): I was, you were
title.it: Was, were (il passato di be): I was, you were

rule.en:
The past of **be** has two forms. **was** for **I**, **he**, **she** and **it**: **I was at the inn.** **Jack was on the fell.** **were** for **you**, **we** and **they**, and **you were** for one person too: **You were late, Sam!** **We were tired.**

No: **wasn't** (was not), **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** **They weren't at home.**

To ask, **was** or **were** goes first: **Was it cold?** **Were you at the show?** The short answer: **Yes, I was.** **No, they weren't.** (never *Yes, I were*, never *Yes, I wasn't*).

With a time that is over: **yesterday**, **last night**, **last week**, **on Monday**, **two days ago**, **this morning**: **I was in Keswick yesterday.**

**there was** for one thing, **there were** for more: **There was a dance at the inn.** **There were a lot of people.**

**Where were you?** asks for a place: **where** and **were** are two words. **born** goes with **was** and **were**: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** **Jack was born on the farm.** (never *Jack is born on the farm.*)
rule.sl:
Preteklik od **be** ima dve obliki. **was** za **I**, **he**, **she** in **it**: **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack je bil na hribu.) **were** za **you**, **we** in **they**, **you were** tudi za eno osebo: **You were late, Sam!** (Zamudil si, Sam!) **We were tired.** (Bili smo utrujeni.)

Zanikanje: **wasn't** (was not), **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Ni bilo mrzlo.) **They weren't at home.** (Niso bili doma.)

Za vprašanje gre **was** ali **were** na začetek: **Was it cold?** (Je bilo mrzlo?) **Were you at the show?** (Si bil{m:|f:a} na sejmu?) Kratki odgovor: **Yes, I was.** **No, they weren't.** Nikoli *Yes, I were*.

S časom, ki je mimo: **yesterday** (včeraj), **last night** (sinoči), **last week** (prejšnji teden), **two days ago** (pred dvema dnevoma), **this morning** (danes zjutraj).

**there was** za eno, **there were** za več: **There was a dance at the inn.** (V gostilni je bil ples.) **There were a lot of people.** (Bilo je veliko ljudi.)

**Where were you?** (Kje si bil{m:|f:a}?): **where** je kje, **were** je be. **born** gre z was: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Teta Edna se je rodila leta 1952.), nikoli *is born*.
rule.de:
Die Vergangenheit von **be** hat zwei Formen. **was** für **I**, **he**, **she** und **it**: **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack war am Berg.) **were** für **you**, **we** und **they**, **you were** auch für eine Person: **You were late, Sam!** (Du warst spät dran, Sam!) **We were tired.** (Wir waren müde.)

Verneinung: **wasn't** (was not), **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Es war nicht kalt.) **They weren't at home.**

In der Frage kommt **was** oder **were** nach vorn: **Was it cold?** (War es kalt?) **Were you at the show?** (Warst du bei der Schau?) Die Kurzantwort: **Yes, I was.** **No, they weren't.** Nie *Yes, I were*.

Mit einer Zeit, die vorbei ist: **yesterday** (gestern), **last night** (gestern Abend), **last week** (letzte Woche), **two days ago** (vor zwei Tagen), **this morning** (heute Morgen).

**there was** für eins, **there were** für mehrere: **There was a dance at the inn.** (Im Gasthaus war Tanz.) **There were a lot of people.** (Es waren viele Leute da.)

Vorsicht: **where** heißt wo, nicht wer! **Where were you?** (Wo warst du?) **born** geht mit was: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Tante Edna ist 1952 geboren.), nie *is born*.
rule.it:
Il passato di **be** ha due forme. **was** (ero, sono stato) per **I**, **he**, **she** e **it**: **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack era sul monte.) **were** per **you**, **we** e **they**, **you were** anche per una persona sola: **You were late, Sam!** (Eri in ritardo, Sam!) **We were tired.** (Eravamo stanchi.)

Il no: **wasn't** (was not), **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Non faceva freddo.) **They weren't at home.** (Non erano a casa.)

Per chiedere, **was** o **were** va all'inizio: **Was it cold?** (Faceva freddo?) **Were you at the show?** (Eri alla fiera?) La risposta breve: **Yes, I was.** **No, they weren't.** Mai *Yes, I were*.

Con un tempo passato: **yesterday** (ieri), **last night** (ieri sera), **last week** (la settimana scorsa), **two days ago** (due giorni fa), **this morning** (stamattina).

**there was** (c'era) per uno, **there were** (c'erano) per più: **There was a dance at the inn.** (C'era un ballo alla locanda.) **There were a lot of people.** (C'era tanta gente.)

**Where were you?** (Dov'eri?): **where** è dove, **were** è be. **born** va con was: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Zia Edna è nata nel 1952.), mai *is born*.
